title: Derived Hom pushforward on fixed K-flat and K-injective representatives
statement: Let i:Z -> Y be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with any supplied derived category D(O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume the tensor pullback i* [def-pc-module-pullback] is additive. Let P be a K-flat cochain complex of O_Y-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex] and J a K-injective cochain complex of O_Z-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Write F for termwise ordinary module pushforward and T=i*P termwise. Then RHom_Y(Q(P),Q(F(J))) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is isomorphic to Q(F(Hom(T,J))) [def-pur-hom-complex] in the supplied D(O_Y). The theorem does not require a specified derived category on Z or a closed immersion.

proof.text: When the derived categories on Z and Y share a localization universe, use the specification of exists_derivedPullback. Its underived representative functor equals the recorded tensor pullback by Functor.ext, and its counit is an isomorphism on P. Compose with the quotient/homotopy comparison isomorphisms to obtain Li*Q(P) isomorphic to Q(T).

Pullback preserves K-flatness, so T is K-flat. Hom(T,J) is K-injective. The direct-image resolution computation at the identity quasi-isomorphisms of J and Hom(T,J) represents their derived direct images by their actual termwise pushforwards.

Apply the supplied internal-Hom pullback/direct-image adjunction isomorphism d at (Q(P),Q(J)). Replace Ri*Q(J) by Q(F(J)). The internal-Hom representative theorem replaces RHom_Z(Li*Q(P),Q(J)) by Q(Hom(T,J)), using the comparison from step 1 and K-injectivity of J. Apply Ri* to this isomorphism and finish with the computation from step 2. This is the complete private same-localization proof.

Choose standard localizations on Z and Y and apply the preceding proof there. Mathlib Localization.uniq and compUniqFunctor compare the standard Q on Y with the supplied Q. Compute internal Hom in both localizations using the same functorial K-injective replacement I of F(J); the two derivedInternalHom_comparison components identify both Hom objects with Q of the identical complex Hom(P,I(F(J))). The Q comparison transports the standard isomorphism back to the supplied category. Compose these explicit isomorphisms; no hypothesis about the supplied universe or localization on Z is introduced.

from.place: Finite-duality branch, quotient-coefficient Koszul calculation: common resolution models for the self-Ext Hom computation and the self-Tor tensor computation, before evaluation or conormal comparison. Specifically steps 1 and 3: fixed K-flat/K-injective comparisons before taking homology.

lean.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedHom_pushforward_kFlat_model
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [hY : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).Additive]
    (P : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) (J : CochainComplex Z.Modules ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := Y.sheaf) P) (hJ : J.IsKInjective) :
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let T := ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P
    Nonempty (((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.sheaf).obj
      (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P), DerivedCategory.Q.obj (F.obj J))) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (F.obj (homComplex (R := Z.sheaf) T J)))
